rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heavy fan-out prompts get body recovery callout

The read can fan out.** If Claude starts reading dozens of files, interrupt with `Esc`, narrow to one feature or directory, and say `continue`." — the maintainer's own framing ("can fan out") self-identifies this as a fan-out-risk prompt, but the callout names only the over-reading direction. It does not name the premature-stop direction (a shallow, single-glance read reported as "done") that rule 48 requires to be named explicitly alongside it.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: If treated as fan-out-eligible (author's own framing suggests yes): add a one-clause premature-stop nudge (e.g. "a report after one file isn't a map either — if the read wraps fast on a big repo, say 'there's more here, keep going'"), distinct from prompt-1's own 'don't try to be complete' self-limiting instruction, which licenses selectivity but not a too-thin read. Note the identical one-direction shape recurs in sibling exercises (fix-tests-first, compound-and-close) — a system-wide fix may be more appropriate than a single-file patch; flag for maintainer to decide scope.
